title: Add benchmark-lab performance suites, profiling baselines, representative runners, and reporting pipeline
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: consolidate benchmark-lab test suites and reporting to produce stable profiling baselines and representative workload runners for common inference shapes. This PR adds: 1) new performance test suites (latency, p50/p95/p99, memory, cold-start), 2) profiling baselines for a set of canonical models and sequence lengths, 3) representative workload runners (chat, completion, embedding, reranking) implemented as reusable runners, and 4) a reporting pipeline that aggregates results into S3 + generates HTML summary reports for the Benchmark Lab dashboard. Implementation notes: - Runners follow the existing runner API used by benchmark-lab and are implemented in benchmark-lab/runners/{chat,completion,embed,rerank}. Each runner includes a CI-friendly smoke test and an optional load generator config. - Profiling baselines are recorded under benchmark-lab/baselines/{model}-{seq}.yml and include kernel timings, memory peaks, and cold-start snapshots. - New test suites are in benchmark-lab/suites/* and use our adaptive-batching harness to exercise batching policies. - Reporting pipeline adds a lightweight step function + lambda (in infra/benchmark-reports) that collects artifacts, computes aggregates, and uploads an HTML report + JSON summary to s3://redwood-benchmark-lab/reports/{date}/. - Documentation and quickstart in benchmark-lab/README.md and redwood-docs/docs/benchmark-lab.md. Checklist: - [x] Implement runners and smoke tests - [x] Add profiling baseline format and example baselines - [x] Wire reporting pipeline and add infra terraform module - [x] Add docs and quickstart - [x] CI green (unit/test integration) - [x] Load testing on staging (small-scale) Testing: ran full benchmark suite on staging (r3-small) for three models (redwood-large-v1, open-llama-7b, mixtral) across seq lengths 128/512/1024. Collected baselines and compared to historical profiles; no regressions >5% observed. Backwards compatibility: runners implement the same runner interface; pipeline is opt-in and behind feature flag BENCHMARK_REPORTS_ENABLED. Related Linear items: ENG-3412 (benchmark lab baseline work), ENG-3499 (reporting infra), ENG-3520 (representative runners).
